name: Mariáš
description: Mariáš is the national card game of the Czech Republic and Slovakia, derived from the historical Mariagespiel. It is a highly competitive trick-taking and bidding game typically played by three players with a 32-card German-suited deck. The game involves complex bidding for different contracts (Standard, Seven, Betl, Durch) and is famous for its strict play rules: you must follow suit, you must trump, and you must win the trick if possible.

content.text: Mariáš is the national card game of the Czech Republic and Slovakia, derived from the historical Mariagespiel. It is a highly competitive trick-taking and bidding game typically played by three players with a 32-card German-suited deck. The game involves complex bidding for different contracts (Standard, Seven, Betl, Durch) and is famous for its strict play rules: you must follow suit, you must trump, and you must win the trick if possible.
Developed from 18th-century Austrian/German games, it solidified into its current 'Marias' form in the Czech lands during the 19th century.
3 players. One is the 'Declarer' (Solo), playing against the other two (Defenders).
Dealer deals 12-10-10 cards or 7-5-5-5-5-5. The declarer gets a 'Talon' (2 cards) to discard.

items.text: Suit: Ordinary game with trumps. Declarer aims to take more card points than the two defenders together. Bonuses for seven (last trick with trump 7), 100+ points, and marriages (king+over).
Betl: No trumps. Declarer must lose every trick to win. Opponents win if they force the declarer to take any trick.
Durch: No trumps. Declarer must win every trick. If opponents take any trick, declarer loses.
Open Betl: Like Betl but after the first trick the declarer's cards are placed face up; all remaining cards must be the lowest outstanding in their suits.
Open Durch: Like Durch but after the first trick the declarer's cards are face up; all remaining must be the highest outstanding in their suits.
